June 17 recap: Northwest Indiana news you may have missed today
Don't miss Wednesday's most popular stories from The Times.
(10) updates to this series since
In honor of dairy month, the LaPorte County Historical Society Museum is featuring an exhibit on historic dairy farms in the Region.
Days after being crowned IHSAA Class 4A state champion, Lake Central junior pitcher Maddie Such was named MaxPreps' 2026 Indiana Softball Player of the Year on Wednesday.
The 134 traffic stops resulted in dozens of citations, warnings and one traffic-related arrest, according to police. Multiple city police departments worked alongside the sheriff's department Wednesday morning.
From flower farms to high tunnels, the NWI Food Council's upcoming FarmHop tour will show community members how local farmers are "pushing the boundaries" of what small-scale farming looks like in the Region.
One handgun was reportedly recovered underneath a young child who was sitting in a child safety seat, with one round in the chamber and no external safety, police said.
Fleetwood Mac, Beatles, Grateful Dead and Dave Matthews tribute bands are headed to Gabis Arboretum at Purdue Northwest this summer.
Although 99% of outages caused by the severe storms and tornadoes on June 11 have been restored, some customers may not have power back on until Friday.
"We want to earn people's trust," Microsoft President Brad Smith said of concerned residents on Wednesday as the city broke ground on its data center.
A flash flood warning was issued for portions of Lake County. Here are some safety tips on what to do if caught in a flood.
Police were notified through the county's Flock camera system that the stolen vehicle was reported near Michigan City.
summary: Days after being crowned IHSAA Class 4A state champion, Lake Central junior pitcher Maddie Such was named MaxPreps' 2026 Indiana Softball Player of the Year on Wednesday. Fleetwood Mac, Beatles, Grateful Dead and Dave Matthews tribute bands are headed to Gabis Arboretum at Purdue Northwest this summer. Although 99% of outages caused by the severe storms and tornadoes on June 11 have been restored, some customers may not have power back on until Friday. "We want to earn people's trust," Microsoft President Brad Smith said of concerned residents on Wednesday as the city broke ground on its data center.
